AST repair, fix, and postprocessing.

Mostly used internally when some AST pieces are built without knowing their target scope/parent, especially during bottom-up construction of AST. The associated symbols, parent and scope pointers cannot be set on construction then. A set of utility functions are provided to patch up scope, parent, symbol for them when the target scope/parent become know.

Detailed Description

Auto-generated documentation for the SageInterface namespace.

Functions that are useful when operating on the AST.

The Sage III IR design attempts to be minimalist. Thus additional functionality is intended to be presented using separate higher level interfaces which work with the IR. This namespace collects functions that operate on the IR and support numerous types of operations that are common to general analysis and transformation of the AST.

Function Documentation

◆ acceptsArguments() [1/2]

bool SageInterface::acceptsArguments ( SgFunctionDeclaration * decl,
std::list< SgType * > args,
bool allowDefaultArgs = true )
static

Checks if a function declaration is compatible with a given list of argument types.

This function validates whether a function declaration can accept a specific list of arguments by comparing the base types of the parameters in the declaration against the provided list of argument types. It also checks for parameter count mismatches and ensures that if default arguments are not allowed, all parameters in the declaration are accounted for in the argument list.

Parameters
declA pointer to the SgFunctionDeclaration representing the function to be checked.

Adds an explicit default constructor to a class if one is missing and other constructors exist.

This function inspects the members of a given class type to determine if a default constructor is present. In C++, if a class defines any constructor, the compiler will not automatically generate a default constructor. This function identifies if such a situation exists (where a constructor is found but no parameterless constructor is found) and, if so, uses SageBuilder to create and prepend a new default constructor to the class definition. It also handles the marking of the new constructor for unparsing based on the provided physical file ID.

Precondition
classType must not be NULL.
The class associated with classType must have a valid SgClassDeclaration, a defining declaration, and a corresponding SgClassDefinition.
Postcondition
If a default constructor was required, the class definition will contain a new public SgMemberFunctionDeclaration acting as a default constructor, prepended to the member list.
Note
The physical_file_id is utilized so that the newly injected constructor can be marked to be unparsed when header file unparsing is active.
The function uses define DEBUG_ADD_DEFAULT_CONSTRUCTOR to control debug logging.

Adds or updates a mangled name in the global cache for a given AST node.

This function manages the mapping between AST nodes and their corresponding mangled names. It handles the logic for generating "short" mangled names using a SHA256-based hash (Base62 encoded) when the original name exceeds a certain length, provided that short names are enabled in the SgProject configuration. If short names are disabled, it preserves the original name. The function also updates the global mangled name map maintained by SgNode.

Parameters

Postcondition

Note
If ifdef DEBUG_MANGLED_SHORTNAME is active, the function performs a collision check using a static map to ensure that different long names do not map to the same 64-bit hash ID.
Using the "short name" feature (where names are truncated/hashed) may cause issues with functions containing special characters (e.g., conversion operators) if the substring/hashing logic alters the recognizable structure.

◆ addStepToLoopBody()

ROSE_DLL_API void SageInterface::addStepToLoopBody ( SgScopeStatement * loopStmt,
SgStatement * step )

Appends a new statement as a step to the body of a loop statement.

Add a step statement to the end of a loop body Add a new label to the end of the loop, with the step statement after it; then change all continue statements in the old loop body into jumps to the label

For example: while (a < 5) {if (a < -3) continue;} (adding "a++" to end) becomes while (a < 5) {if (a < -3) goto label; label: a++;}

This function modifies the control flow of an existing loop by inserting a new statement (step) into the loop body. The implementation creates a new basic block and a unique label. It transforms existing 'continue' statements within the original loop body into 'goto' statements that target the newly created label. This ensures that the loop's execution flow is redirected through the new step before proceeding. The function utilizes a global or static gensym_counter to ensure the uniqueness of the generated label name.

Parameters
loopStmtA pointer to the SgScopeStatement representing the loop to be modified.
stepA pointer to the SgStatement that is to be added as a new step within the loop's execution flow.
Precondition
loopStmt must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgScopeStatement.
step must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgStatement.
Postcondition
The loop body of loopStmt is updated to include the new basic block containing the step and the label.
Any 'continue' statements in the original loop body are redirected to the new label.
Note
This function relies on the existence of SageBuilder namespace functions such as buildBasicBlock, buildLabelStatement, and appendStatement.
The label name is generated using a prefix "rose_label__" followed by an incremented counter.

◆ appendStatementWithDependentDeclaration()

ROSE_DLL_API void SageInterface::appendStatementWithDependentDeclaration ( SgDeclarationStatement * decl,
SgGlobal * scope,
SgStatement * original_statement,
bool excludeHeaderFiles )

Append a copy ('decl') of a function ('original_statement') into a 'scope', include any referenced declarations required if the scope is within a compiler generated file. All referenced declarations, including those from headers, are inserted if excludeHeaderFiles is set to true (the new file will not have any headers).

Appends a statement along with its required dependent declarations and preprocessing directives to a new scope.

This function is designed to support the outlining of functions into separate files. When a function (or statement) is moved to a new scope (such as a new file), it often carries dependencies on declarations and preprocessing directives (like include) from its original location. This function identifies those dependencies, generates copies of the dependent declarations in the target scope, and ensures that the AST references are correctly updated using a replacement map to maintain consistency across the new and old AST nodes.

The implementation performs the following steps:

  1. Identifies all declarations that the input decl depends upon using getDependentDeclarations.
  2. Generates copies of these dependent declarations within the target scope.
  3. Builds a replacementMap to map old AST nodes (symbols, scopes, etc.) to their new counterparts in the copied AST.
  4. Collects necessary C++ preprocessing directives (e.g., include) from the original_statement's source file.
  5. Inserts the copied dependent declarations into the target scope ahead of the target decl.
  6. Attaches the required preprocessing directives to the newly inserted declarations, ensuring no redundancy with directives already present on the declarations themselves.
  7. Uses Rose::AST::Utility::edgePointerReplacement to traverse the outlined file and update all pointers in the replacementMap to point to the new nodes.
Parameters
declThe declaration statement that is being moved/outlined.
scopeThe target global scope where the statement and its dependencies will be appended.
original_statementThe original statement from which the dependencies and preprocessing information are being extracted.
excludeHeaderFilesA boolean flag. If true, include directives will not be appended to the new scope.
Precondition
decl must have a valid non-defining declaration.
The source file of decl must match the source file of its first non-defining declaration.
The scope of decl must be the same as the target scope.
original_statement must have a valid global scope.
Postcondition
The target scope contains copies of all declarations that decl depends on.
The target scope contains the necessary preprocessing directives (unless excludeHeaderFiles is true).
The AST pointers within the outlinedFile are updated via edgePointerReplacement to ensure all references point to the new copies of nodes.
Note
This function relies on ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT not being defined for the primary logic to execute.
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT extensively to ensure the integrity of the AST transformation.
Support for SgTemplateInstantiationDecl and SgMemberFunctionDeclaration as dependent declarations is currently not implemented and will trigger a ROSE_ABORT.

Compute the intersection set for two ASTs.

Finds the intersection of nodes between an original AST and its copy.

This is part of a test done by the copy function to compute those IR nodes in the copy that still reference the original AST.

This function identifies the set of IR nodes that are common to both the original Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) and a provided copy of the AST. It performs a deep comparison by querying subtrees, computing the set intersection of all nodes, and filtering out specific node types (such as SgType) that are permitted to be shared between the two trees. Additionally, if a SgCopyHelp object is provided, the function validates the mapping between original and copied nodes to ensure structural consistency.

Parameters

copyA pointer to the root node of the copied AST.
helpA pointer to a SgCopyHelp object containing the mapping between original and copied nodes, used for verifying node correspondence.
Returns

Precondition
The original and copy pointers should point to valid SgNode trees.
Postcondition
The returned vector contains nodes present in both trees, excluding nodes identified as SgType.
Warning
If the number of nodes in the original AST and the copy differ, the function prints a warning. If there are unmatched IR nodes (nodes in the original that do not have a corresponding entry in the help map) and the sizes are different, the function will trigger a ROSE_ABORT().
Note
The function uses std::set_intersection to perform the core comparison logic. It also relies on SgProject::get_verbose() to control the level of diagnostic output to the console.

Similarly, if the scope corresponds to a namespace definition named "B", the symbol table of that namespace is printed.

◆ checkTypesAreEqual()

bool SageInterface::checkTypesAreEqual ( SgType * typeA,
SgType * typeB )

Determines if two SgType objects are equivalent.

This function performs a deep comparison of two types to check for structural and semantic equality. It utilizes an internal helper class, TypeEquivalenceChecker, to traverse the type hierarchies. The comparison accounts for various type categories including named types, pointer types, reference types, array types, and function types.

The implementation handles the following logic:

  • If both pointers are identical, they are considered equal.
  • For typedefs, the function can strip the typedef to compare the underlying base types.
  • For modifier types (e.g., const, volatile, restrict), it compares the const and volatile qualifiers. If semantic equivalence is enabled, it can strip volatile and restrict modifiers to compare the base types.
  • For named types, it compares their qualified names, provided they are not autonomous declarations.
  • For pointer and reference types, it recursively checks the equality of the base types.
  • For array types, it checks both the equality of the base types and the equivalence of the array indices (if they are constant integer expressions).
  • For function types, it verifies that the return types are equal and that the argument lists have the same size and identical argument types.

The function relies on the include of RoseAst for AST traversal and include of SgType definitions. It uses ifndef USE_CMAKEx to ensure compatibility with the build system's AST traversal capabilities.

Parameters
typeAA pointer to the first SgType to be compared.
typeBA pointer to the second SgType to be compared.
Returns
True if the two types are considered equal under the implemented equivalence rules; false otherwise. Returns false if either input pointer is NULL.
Precondition
typeA and typeB should be valid SgType pointers, or NULL.
Postcondition
The equality status of the provided types is determined without modifying the underlying type structures.
Note
If the function is compiled without USE_CMAKEx, the function will trigger a ROSE_ABORT().
The internal TypeEquivalenceChecker can be configured to use semantic equivalence, which affects how modifiers like volatile and restrict are handled.

◆ cleanupNontransformedBasicBlockNode()

ROSE_DLL_API void SageInterface::cleanupNontransformedBasicBlockNode ( )

Remove unused basic block IR nodes added as part of normalization.

Removes unused basic block IR nodes added during the normalization process.

This function iterates through a collection of added basic block nodes (addedBasicBlockNodes) and attempts to "denormalize" them. If a basic block contains exactly one statement, the function attempts to bypass the basic block by re-linking the single statement directly to its parent statement (such as an if-statement, while-loop, or switch-case). This is used to support higher quality token-based unparsing by cleaning up intermediate IR nodes that were only necessary for normalization.

The function handles various statement types including V_SgIfStmt, V_SgWhileStmt, V_SgSwitchStatement, V_SgForStatement, V_SgCaseOptionStmt, V_SgDefaultOptionStmt, and V_SgDoWhileStmt. It also manages the isModified flag of the parent node to ensure that if the modification was solely due to this cleanup, the flag is reset.

Precondition
The addedBasicBlockNodes vector must be initialized.
Postcondition
Basic blocks containing only one statement are bypassed in the IR tree where possible, and the parent statement is updated to point directly to the inner statement.
Note
This function should be called before the unparse step.
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate that blocks and statements are not NULL.
If an unhandled statement variant is encountered during the cleanup of a single-statement block, the function will call ROSE_ABORT().

◆ convertForToWhile()

ROSE_DLL_API void SageInterface::convertForToWhile ( SgForStatement * f)

Transforms a for-loop statement into a while-loop statement.

This function performs a structural transformation of a given for-loop (SgForStatement) into a while-loop (SgWhileStmt). The process involves extracting the loop increment logic and moving it into the loop body, creating a new basic block to host the initialization statements, and constructing a while-loop that uses the original loop test condition. The original for-loop is then replaced in its parent statement list by the newly created basic block containing the initialization.

Parameters
fA pointer to the SgForStatement to be converted.
Precondition
The parameter f must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgForStatement.
The parent of the SgForStatement must be a valid SgStatement that allows statement replacement.
Postcondition
The original SgForStatement is replaced by a new basic block in the parent statement list.
The loop increment logic from the original for-loop is moved into the loop body.
A new SgWhileStmt is appended to the newly created basic block.
Note
This transformation assumes that the loop body can accommodate the moved increment statement without violating the intended semantics of the original loop.
If the for-loop has an empty condition, a dummy true-value expression statement is used as the while-loop test.

Variable references can be introduced by SgVarRef, SgPntrArrRefExp, SgInitializedName, SgMemberFunctionRef etc. For Dot and Arrow Expressions, their lhs is used to obtain SgInitializedName (coarse grain) by default. Otherwise, fine-grain rhs is used.

Cut preprocessing information from a source node and save it into a buffer. Used in combination of pastePreprocessingInfo(). The cut-paste operation is similar to moveUpPreprocessingInfo() but it is more flexible in that the destination node can be unknown during the cut operation.

Cut preprocessing information from a source node and save it into a buffer. Used in combination of pastePreprocessingInfo(). The cut-paste operation is similar to moveUpPreprocessingInfo() but it is more flexible in that the destination node only need to be known until the paste action.

Extracts preprocessing information from a source node and stores it in a buffer.

This function performs a "cut" operation on the preprocessing information attached to a specific source node. It identifies preprocessing elements that do not satisfy a relative position requirement based on the provided position type and moves them from the source node's attached information into the provided buffer. This is designed to be used in conjunction with pastePreprocessingInfo(). The logic is similar to moveUpPreprocessingInfo() but offers greater flexibility because the destination for the information is not required until the subsequent paste action occurs.

The implementation iterates through the attached preprocessing information of the src_node. Elements that do not satisfy the isRelPos condition (where isRelPos returns false) are copied to the save_buf. Subsequently, elements that do satisfy the isRelPos condition are removed from the source node's information container.

Parameters
src_nodeA pointer to the SgLocatedNode from which the preprocessing information is to be cut. Must not be null.
posThe relative position type used to determine which preprocessing elements should be moved to the buffer.
save_bufA reference to an AttachedPreprocessingInfoType container where the extracted preprocessing information will be stored.
Precondition
src_node must not be null.
Postcondition
The preprocessing information in src_node is modified such that elements matching the relative position criteria are removed, and those that do not match are appended to save_buf.
Note
This function relies on the existence of attached preprocessing information within the src_node. If no information is attached, the function performs no action.

The function collects all SgNode pointers during the traversal and subsequently iterates through the collected list to explicitly call the delete operator on each node. The function uses a post-order traversal strategy to ensure that child nodes and dependent symbols are processed before their parents, preventing dangling pointers.

The implementation specifically handles the safe removal of:

  • Type information and symbol references.

This function performs a deep deletion of an AST subtree starting from the provided root node. The implementation utilizes a custom internal visitor class inheriting from AstSimpleProcessing. The traversal follows a postorder pattern to ensure that child nodes are processed before their parents. Specifically, for every node encountered, the function checks if it is an SgExpression. If it is, the visitor recursively traverses the tree associated with the original expression (retrieved via get_originalExpressionTree()) before deleting the current node. This ensures that nested original expression trees are properly deallocated.

Parameters
rootA pointer to the root SgNode of the tree to be deleted.
Precondition
The root pointer must be a valid pointer to an SgNode or NULL.
Postcondition
The memory associated with the root node, its children, and any linked original expression trees is deallocated. The root pointer becomes dangling.
Note
This function relies on the postorder traversal to prevent memory leaks in the hierarchy of original expression trees.

◆ detectCycleInType()

void SageInterface::detectCycleInType ( SgType * type,
const std::string & from )

Detects if there is a circular dependency or cycle within a type definition.

This function traverses the underlying base types of a given SgType (including modifiers, pointers, references, arrays, and typedefs) to check for recursive type definitions that would result in an infinite loop. It maintains a list of previously visited types in a vector. If a type is encountered that has already been seen in the current traversal path, a cycle is identified, an error message is printed detailing the path of the cycle, and the program is aborted.

Parameters
typeThe SgType pointer to the type being inspected for cycles.
fromA string representing the call site or context from which this detection function was invoked, used for error reporting.
Warning
If a cycle is detected, the function calls ROSE_ABORT(), which terminates the program execution.
Precondition
The parameter type should ideally not be NULL, although the function contains a loop condition to handle NULL termination.
Postcondition
If no cycle is found, the function completes execution normally. If a cycle is found, the program is aborted.
Note
The function uses an iterative approach to strip away type qualifiers (such as const, volatile, pointers, etc.) to reach the fundamental base type.

Prints the details of a given scope statement and its contained statements to the standard output.

This function is intended for debugging purposes. It identifies the scope by its memory address and class name, then iterates through all statements contained within that scope. For each statement, it prints the index, memory address, class name, and the name of the node. The function uses ROSE_ASSERT(scope) to validate the input.

top-down traversal from current node to find the main() function declaration

Searches for the main function declaration within a given node and its descendants.

This function performs a depth-first search through the SgNode hierarchy starting from the provided node n. It checks if the current node is a main function declaration. If the current node is not the main function, the function recursively traverses all children contained within the node's traversal successor container. A specific check is performed to ensure that the found declaration is a defining declaration (i.e., the declaration matches its defining declaration) to avoid returning non-defining main declarations.

Parameters
nThe starting SgNode from which to begin the search for the main function.
Returns
A pointer to the SgFunctionDeclaration representing the main function if found; otherwise, returns 0 (nullptr).

The input node n should be a valid SgNode pointer, though the function handles null pointers gracefully.
Postcondition
If a main function is found, it is returned as an SgFunctionDeclaration pointer. The state of the SgNode tree remains unchanged.
Note
This function uses a recursive traversal strategy. For very deep AST structures, this could potentially lead to stack overflow.

Supporting function to comment relocation in insertStatement() and removeStatement().

Remove a statement: TODO consider side effects for symbol tables.

It first attempts to traverse backwards through the statement sequence (using getPreviousStatement) to find a preceding statement in the same file. If no such statement is found (e.g., reaching the top of the file or global scope), the function performs a second pass traversing forwards (using getNextStatement) to find a following statement in the same file. The function also tracks whether the found statement precedes or follows the target statement via a boolean reference.

Postcondition
The returned SgStatement, if not NULL, will share the same file ID as targetStmt.
The value of surroundingStatementPreceedsTargetStatement is updated to reflect the relative position of the returned statement to targetStmt.
Note
The function uses a set of visited statements to prevent infinite loops during traversal in case of circular statement references.

Fixes the scope and symbol associations for a class declaration.

This function ensures that the structural integrity of a class declaration and its associated non-defining declarations are maintained within the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). It specifically addresses issues arising from bottom-up AST building where scopes might be missing. The function performs the following tasks:

  1. Validates that the provided struct declaration and scope are not null.
  2. Ensures that the struct declaration and its first non-defining declaration are associated with the provided scope if their current scope is null.

  5. Validates that the underlying type is a valid SgClassType and not a generic SgNode.

The type associated with the non-defining declaration must be a valid SgClassType.
Postcondition
If structDecl or its non-defining declaration had a NULL scope, they are updated to point to the provided scope.
If a class symbol was missing in the scope, a new SgClassSymbol is created and inserted into the scope.
The type of the defining declaration (if it exists) is synchronized to match the type of the non-defining declaration.

The function contains logic to handle translation errors where a symbol might be found via lookup but is missing from the symbol table.

◆ forLoopNormalization()

ROSE_DLL_API bool SageInterface::forLoopNormalization ( SgForStatement * loop,
bool foldConstant = true )

Normalizes the components of a for-loop statement.

Normalize a for loop, part of migrating Qing's loop handling into SageInterface.

Normalize a for loop, return true if successful. Generated constants will be fold by default.

Translations are : For the init statement: for (int i=0;... ) becomes int i; for (i=0;..) For test expression: i<x is normalized to i<= (x-1) and i>x is normalized to i>= (x+1) For increment expression: i++ is normalized to i+=1 and i– is normalized to i+=-1 i-=s is normalized to i+= -s

This function performs a multi-step normalization process on a given for-loop statement. It aims to standardize the loop's initialization, test condition, and increment expression. The process involves decomposing the initialization declaration, normalizing the loop test, and normalizing the increment expression. Additionally, it ensures the loop body is contained within a basic block. If the foldConstant flag is set to true, the function performs constant folding specifically on the loop's test and increment expressions to simplify the loop control logic.

Parameters
loopA pointer to the SgForStatement representing the for-loop to be normalized. Must not be NULL.
foldConstantA boolean flag indicating whether constant folding should be applied to the loop's test and increment expressions. Defaults to true.
Returns
Returns true if all normalization steps (initialization, test, increment, and body adjustment) were successful; returns false if any step fails.
Precondition
loop must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The loop's initialization, test, and increment expressions are normalized, and the loop body is guaranteed to be a basic block.
Note
Constant folding is restricted to the loop controlling expressions (test and increment) to prevent potential loss of accuracy in floating-point operations that might occur if the entire loop body were folded.

◆ functionCallExpressionPreceedsDeclarationWhichAssociatesScope()

bool SageInterface::functionCallExpressionPreceedsDeclarationWhichAssociatesScope ( SgFunctionCallExp * functionCall)

Determines if a function call expression occurs before the declaration that establishes its scope.

This function performs a preorder traversal of the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) starting from the global scope to analyze the relative ordering of a specific function call expression and the declaration of the function being called. It specifically checks if the function call appears in the AST before a declaration statement that would associate a specific scope (such as a scope that supports defining function declarations) with the function. This is particularly relevant for the unparser to decide whether name qualification is required.

The implementation utilizes an internal class, DeclarationOrderTraversal, which inherits from AstSimpleProcessing. The traversal identifies the function symbol associated with the provided function call and tracks whether the call is encountered before a declaration that matches the function's non-defining declaration and resides within a scope capable of defining functions.

Parameters
functionCallA pointer to the SgFunctionCallExp representing the function call to be analyzed. The function call must not be NULL and must have a valid function expression.
Returns
Returns true if the function call expression precedes the declaration that associates the scope, or if the function call itself cannot be found within the traversal. Returns false if a declaration that associates the scope is found before the function call.
Precondition
functionCall must not be NULL.
functionCall->get_function() must not be NULL.
The function symbol associated with the function call must have a valid declaration.
Postcondition
The function returns a boolean indicating the relative order of the call and the scope-associating declaration.
Note
The current implementation contains a bypass (via if 0) that skips the actual traversal to avoid O(n^2) complexity during unparsing, effectively simulating a found state.
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate the integrity of the AST nodes during traversal.
Some cases for expression variants (e.g., V_SgDotExp, V_SgArrowExp) are identified but not yet implemented and will trigger a ROSE_ABORT.

◆ generateUniqueNameForUseAsIdentifier_support()

std::string SageInterface::generateUniqueNameForUseAsIdentifier_support ( SgDeclarationStatement * declaration)

Generates a unique, human-readable identifier from a given declaration.

This function creates a string that can be used as a valid C++ identifier, derived from the metadata of a provided SgDeclarationStatement. Unlike standard C++ mangled names, which are compressed and often restricted to a single translation unit, the names generated here are designed to be used across multiple translation units. The generated names explicitly include scope and function information, making them easier to interpret during debugging.

The implementation handles several types of declarations:

  • Class and Template Class Declarations: Constructs a name using the scope and type name.
  • Template Instantiations: Constructs a name and performs character substitution (e.g., replacing '<', '>', ',', '*', and '&' with safe strings like 'abs', 'abe', 'comma', 'star', and 'ref') to ensure the result is a valid identifier.
  • Function and Member Function Declarations: Uses a mangled version of the function name (including return type information) and implements a collision detection mechanism using a local map to append numeric suffixes if a name conflict is detected.
Parameters
declarationA pointer to the SgDeclarationStatement from which the unique name is to be generated.
Returns
A string representing a unique, valid C++ identifier derived from the input declaration.
Precondition
The declaration parameter must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The returned string is a valid C++ identifier suitable for use in DSL infrastructure and cross-translation unit references.
Note
The function currently only supports class declarations, template class declarations, template instantiations, and function/member function declarations. Other declaration types are treated as unsupported.
The function relies on an external local_name_collision_map to track and resolve name collisions for functions.

◆ getDeclarationOfNamedFunction()

SgFunctionDeclaration * SageInterface::getDeclarationOfNamedFunction ( SgExpression * func)

Retrieves the function declaration associated with a given function expression.

Given a SgExpression that represents a named function (or bound member function), return the mentioned function

This function attempts to resolve a function declaration from an SgExpression. It handles different types of expressions, specifically checking if the expression is a direct function reference or a member function access via dot or arrow operators.

The implementation follows these steps:

  1. Checks if the expression is a simple function reference expression. If so, it retrieves the declaration from the underlying symbol.
  2. If the expression is a dot or arrow operator expression, it inspects the right-hand side operand. If the right-hand side is a member function reference expression, it retrieves the declaration from that symbol.
  3. If the right-hand side of a member access is not a member function reference, a warning is printed to stderr.
Parameters
funcA pointer to the SgExpression representing the function or member function access to be resolved.
Returns
A pointer to the SgFunctionDeclaration associated with the expression, or NULL if no valid declaration can be found or if the expression type is unsupported.
Warning
If a dot or arrow expression is encountered where the right-hand side operand is not a member function reference, a warning message is sent to cerr containing the class name of the invalid operand.
Precondition
The input parameter func should not be a null pointer.
Postcondition
The function returns a valid SgFunctionDeclaration pointer if the expression is a valid function reference or member function access; otherwise, it returns NULL.
Note
This function relies on the helper functions isSgFunctionRefExp, isSgDotExp, isSgArrowExp, isSgBinaryOp, and isSgMemberFunctionRefExp to perform type checking and operand extraction.

◆ getEnclosingNode()

template<typename NodeType>
NodeType * SageInterface::getEnclosingNode ( const SgNode * astNode,

Finds the nearest ancestor of a given AST node that matches a specified type.

Find a node by type using upward traversal.

Traverse backward through a specified node's ancestors, starting with the node's parent and progressing to more distant ancestors, to find the first node matching the specified or derived type. If includingSelf is true then the starting node, astNode, is returned if its type matches, otherwise the search starts at the parent of astNode.

For the purposes of this function, the parent (P) of an SgDeclarationStatement node (N) is considered to be the first non-defining declaration of N if N has both a defining declaration and a first non-defining declaration and the defining declaration is different than the first non-defining declaration.

If no ancestor of the requisite type of subtypes is found then this function returns a null pointer.

If astNode is the null pointer, then the return value is a null pointer. That is, if there is no node, then there cannot be an enclosing node of the specified type.

This function traverses the upward hierarchy of the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) starting from the provided node. It searches for the first node in the ancestry chain that can be dynamically cast to the template parameter NodeType. The traversal accounts for special cases in the ROSE AST, such as SgDeclarationStatement, where the traversal may jump to a defining declaration instead of simply moving to the immediate parent.

The implementation includes cycle detection using a std::set of previously visited nodes to prevent infinite loops caused by malformed AST structures or complex declaration relationships.

includingSelfA boolean flag indicating whether the search should include the astNode itself as a potential match. Defaults to false.
Returns

◆ getFrontendSpecificNodes()

ROSE_DLL_API std::set< SgNode * > SageInterface::getFrontendSpecificNodes ( )

Retrieves a set of SgNodes that are uniquely identified as frontend-specific.

This function performs a traversal of the SgNode hierarchy to identify nodes that belong to the frontend-specific category. It utilizes an internal visitor class, FrontendSpecificTraversal, which inherits from ROSE_VisitTraversal.

The implementation works by traversing the graph and categorizing nodes into two sets: specific and non_specific, based on the properties found in their Sg_File_Info. The traversal includes a recursive collection step via recursive_collect that follows data member pointers to ensure that all reachable nodes associated with a specific node are also evaluated. Finally, the function computes the set difference between the specific and non_specific sets to isolate nodes that are strictly frontend-specific and not shared with the general infrastructure.

Precondition
The SgNode hierarchy must be valid and traversable.
Postcondition
Returns a std::set containing only those SgNode* pointers that are marked as frontend-specific and are not present in the non-specific set.
Note
The internal recursive_collect function implements a cycle-detection mechanism by checking if a node has already been inserted into the collection to prevent infinite loops during traversal.

◆ getLiveVariables()

ROSE_DLL_API void SageInterface::getLiveVariables ( LivenessAnalysis * liv,
SgForStatement * loop,
std::set< SgInitializedName * > & liveIns,
std::set< SgInitializedName * > & liveOuts )

get liveIn and liveOut variables for a for loop from liveness analysis result liv.

Get liveIn and liveOut variables for a for loop.

Retrieves the live-in and live-out variables for a specific for loop.

This function identifies the set of variables that are live at the entry (live-in) and exit (live-out) of a given SgForStatement. The implementation traverses the Control Flow Graph (CFG) to locate the specific CFG node corresponding to the loop's conditional test (the node with two outgoing edges: one for the true branch and one for the false branch).

The live-in variables of the loop are determined by the live-in variables of the first statement inside the loop body (the target of the true edge). The live-out variables of the loop are determined by the live-in variables of the first statement following the loop (the target of the false edge).

Parameters
livA pointer to the LivenessAnalysis object used to query the live-in sets of CFG nodes.
loopA pointer to the SgForStatement node for which the liveness analysis is being performed.
liveInsA reference to a set of SgInitializedName pointers that will be populated with the variables live at the start of the loop.
liveOutsA reference to a set of SgInitializedName pointers that will be populated with the variables live at the end of the loop.
Precondition
liv must not be NULL.
loop must not be NULL.
The CFG node associated with the loop must have exactly two outgoing edges representing the true and false branches of the loop condition.
Postcondition
The liveIns set contains all SgInitializedName elements that are live at the loop entry.
The liveOuts set contains all SgInitializedName elements that are live at the loop exit.
Note
The function relies on a specific CFG node index (index 2) to correctly identify the loop test node within the CFG structure.
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate the integrity of the input pointers and the CFG edge count.

◆ HasNoThrowAssign()

bool SageInterface::HasNoThrowAssign ( const SgType *const inputType)

Determines whether a given type has an assignment operator that is guaranteed not to throw exceptions.

This function analyzes the provided SgType to check if its assignment operation is exception-safe. The implementation first strips typedefs and array decorations from the input type. It then checks if the underlying type is const or a reference, in which case it cannot have a non-throwing assignment in the traditional sense. If the type has a trivial assignment, it returns true. For class types, the function traverses the entire class hierarchy to inspect all member functions. It specifically looks for an 'operator=' implementation and verifies if it possesses the GNU 'nothrow' attribute.

Parameters
inputTypeA pointer to the SgType to be analyzed.
Returns
True if the type's assignment operator is guaranteed not to throw (e.g., trivial assignment or explicitly marked with noexcept/nothrow attribute); false otherwise.
Precondition
inputType must not be a null pointer.
Postcondition
The state of the inputType is not modified, though internal stripping of typedefs and arrays is performed on a temporary pointer derived from inputType.
Note
This implementation currently relies on checking the GNU attribute for no-throw specifications. Support for C++11 'noexcept' expressions is a known TODO.
The function uses ifdef DEBUG_QUADRATIC_BEHAVIOR to optionally print debugging information regarding the number of member functions scanned.

bool SageInterface::hasUpcSharedType ( SgType * t,

Has a UPC shared type of any kinds (shared-to-shared, private-to-shared, shared-to-private, shared scalar/array)? An optional parameter, mod_type_out, stores the first SgModifierType with UPC access information.

Checks if a given SgType contains a UPC shared modifier type.

Has a UPC shared type?

Note: we classify private-to-shared as 'has shared' type for convenience here. It is indeed a private type in strict sense. AST graph for some examples:

  • shared scalar: SgModifierType -->base type
  • shared array: SgArrayType --> SgModiferType --> base type
  • shared to shared: SgModifierType --> SgPointerType --> SgModifierType ->SgTypeInt
  • shared to private: SgModifierType --> SgPointerType --> base type
  • private to shared: SgPointerType --> SgModifierType --> base type

This function recursively traverses the type hierarchy of a given SgType (including pointers, references, arrays, typedefs, and modifier types) to determine if any level of the type definition contains a UPC shared modifier. If a shared modifier is found, the pointer to that modifier is optionally returned via the output parameter.

Parameters
sg_typeA pointer to the SgType to be inspected.
mod_type_outA pointer to a pointer of type SgModifierType. If provided, it will be set to the discovered UPC shared modifier type if found, or NULL if no such type exists.
Returns
True if a UPC shared modifier type is found within the type hierarchy; otherwise, false.
Precondition
sg_type must not be NULL.
Postcondition
If mod_type_out is not NULL, it will point to the discovered SgModifierType on success, or be set to NULL if no shared type is found.
Note
The function uses a recursive approach to navigate through base types of pointers, references, arrays, and typedefs.

Checks if a given type has a virtual destructor.

This function determines whether the specified SgType represents a class that possesses a virtual destructor. The implementation first strips typedef and array attributes from the input type to reach the underlying base type. It then verifies if the resulting type is a class. If it is, the function traverses the entire class hierarchy to inspect all member function declarations. It searches for a member function that is marked as both virtual and as a destructor.

The state of the inputType object remains unchanged, although internal stripping logic is applied to a local pointer.

The function relies on ENSURE_CLASS_TYPE to validate the type after stripping modifiers.

SgCommaOpExp * SageInterface::insertAfterUsingCommaOp ( SgExpression * new_exp,

Insert an expression (new_exp ) after another expression (anchor_exp) has possible side effects, without changing the original semantics. This is done by using two comma operators: type T1; ... ((T1 = anchor_exp, new_exp),T1) )... , where T1 is a temp variable saving the possible side effect of anchor_exp. The top level comma op exp is returned. The reference to T1 in T1 = anchor_exp is saved in temp_ref.

Insert an expression (new_exp ) after another expression (anchor_exp) has possible side effects, with minimum changes to the original semantics. This is done by using two comma operators: type T1; ... ((T1 = anchor_exp, new_exp),T1) )... , where T1 is a temp variable saving the possible side effect of anchor_exp. The top level comma op exp is returned. The reference to T1 in T1 = anchor_exp is saved in temp_ref.

Inserts an expression after an anchor expression using comma operators to preserve side effects.

This function performs a transformation to insert a new expression (new_exp) immediately after an existing expression (anchor_exp) in a way that preserves the original semantics, even if anchor_exp has side effects. The implementation achieves this by introducing a temporary variable T1 of the same type as anchor_exp. It constructs a nested comma operator structure: ((T1 = anchor_exp, new_exp), T1). This ensures that the side effects of anchor_exp are captured in T1, the new_exp is executed, and the final value of the expression remains consistent with the original anchor_exp. A variable declaration for T1 is inserted before the enclosing statement of the anchor_exp.

Parameters
new_expThe expression to be inserted after the anchor expression.
anchor_expThe existing expression that serves as the anchor point for the insertion.
temp_declA pointer to a pointer of SgStatement*. If not NULL, it will be updated to point to the newly created variable declaration statement.
temp_refA pointer to a pointer of SgVarRefExp*. If not NULL, it will be updated to point to the variable reference expression used to access the temporary variable.
Returns
A pointer to the newly constructed SgCommaOpExp that replaces the original anchor_exp.
Precondition
new_exp must not be NULL.
anchor_exp must not be NULL.
new_exp must not be the same as anchor_exp.
anchor_exp must have a non-NULL parent node.
anchor_exp must have a valid type.
anchor_exp must be contained within an enclosing SgStatement.
Postcondition
The anchor_exp is replaced in the AST by a new SgCommaOpExp.
A new variable declaration is inserted before the enclosing statement of the original anchor_exp.
Note
This function uses a global gensym_counter to ensure the uniqueness of the temporary variable name (e.g., _t_1, _t_2).
The implementation uses deepCopy on anchor_exp during the assignment construction to prevent unintended side effects on the original AST structure during the transformation.

This function creates a new PreprocessingInfo object containing an #include directive for the specified filename. The function searches for an appropriate statement within the provided scope (or the global scope if scope is NULL) to attach the preprocessing information to. It handles complexities related to token-based unparsing by marking surrounding whitespace as modified and manages scope adjustments when inserting headers into header files (e.g., .tcc, .h).

Precondition
The provided scope, if not NULL, must be a valid SgScopeStatement.
The global scope associated with the scope must be accessible and not NULL.
Postcondition
If successful, a PreprocessingInfo object is returned with its file information marked as a transformation.

Note

The function also includes logic to relocate attached preprocessing information (like comments or ifdef directives) from the target statement to the new statement to maintain source fidelity. Insert statements before the first non-declaration statement in a scope. If the scope has no non-declaration statements.

Inserts a list of statements before the first non-declaration statement within a given scope.

This function iterates through the statement list of the provided scope. It searches for the first statement that is not a declaration (using isSgDeclarationStatement). This function relies on the existence of isSgDeclarationStatement, insertStatementListBefore, and appendStatementList within the ROSE framework.

◆ instrumentEndOfFunction()

ROSE_DLL_API int SageInterface::instrumentEndOfFunction ( SgFunctionDeclaration * func,
SgStatement * s )

Instrument(Add a statement, often a function call) into a function right before the return points, handle multiple return statements (with duplicated statement s) and return expressions with side effects. Return the number of statements inserted.

Inserts a given statement before every return statement or at the end of a function.

Useful when adding a runtime library call to terminate the runtime system right before the end of a program, especially for OpenMP and UPC runtime systems. Return with complex expressions with side effects are rewritten using an additional assignment statement.

This function traverses the AST of a function declaration to find all return statements. For each return statement found, it attempts to insert the provided statement s immediately before the return. If the return statement contains an expression that is not a simple value expression, the function attempts to split the expression to ensure the inserted statement does not interfere with the return value. If the function contains no return statements, the statement s is appended to the end of the function body.

Parameters
funcA pointer to the SgFunctionDeclaration representing the function to be instrumented.
sA pointer to the SgStatement that is to be inserted into the function.
Returns
The total number of insertion points created (the number of return statements found, or 1 if the statement was appended to the end of a function without returns).
Precondition
func and s must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The function func is modified such that s (or a copy of s) exists immediately before every SgReturnStmt or at the end of the function body.
Note
If multiple return statements exist, a copy of the statement s is created for subsequent insertions to avoid reusing the same statement object.
If the function body is NULL and no return statements are found, the function will trigger a ROSE_ABORT.

◆ isAncestor()

bool ROSE_DLL_API SageInterface::isAncestor ( SgNode * node1,
SgNode * node2 )

check if node1 is a strict ancestor of node 2. (a node is not considered its own ancestor)

Determines if node1 is an ancestor of node2 in the SgNode hierarchy.

This function checks the structural relationship between two nodes in a Rose Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). It traverses upwards from node2 through its parent pointers to see if node1 is encountered. The function specifically excludes the case where a node is considered an ancestor of itself.

Parameters
node1The potential ancestor node to be checked.
node2The descendant node from which the upward traversal begins.
Returns
True if node1 is a direct or indirect parent of node2, false otherwise.
Precondition
node1 and node2 must not be nullptr.
Postcondition
The function does not modify the state of the provided SgNode objects.
Note
The function uses a loop to traverse the parent chain of node2. The traversal terminates when either node1 is found or the root of the tree (nullptr) is reached.
If node1 and node2 are the same node, the function returns false.

◆ isArrayReference() [2/3]

bool SageInterface::isArrayReference ( SgExpression * ref,
SgExpression ** arrayName )

Checks if an expression is an array access and optionally retrieves its name and subscripts.

This function inspects a given SgExpression to determine if it represents an array reference (specifically of type V_SgPntrArrRefExp). If the expression is an array access, the function can traverse the nested array access structure to extract the base array name and the collection of subscripts used in the access. The traversal works by iteratively moving through the left-hand side operands of the array reference expression.

Parameters
refThe expression to be checked for array reference status.
arrayNameA pointer to a pointer of SgExpression. If not NULL, this will be populated with the SgExpression representing the base array name (the left-hand side operand of the innermost array access).
subscriptsA pointer to a pointer to a vector of SgExpression pointers. If not NULL, this vector will be populated with the subscripts used in the array access, ordered such that the first dimension visited is at the end of the vector (the last visited right-hand side operand is inserted at the beginning).
Returns
True if the expression is an array reference (V_SgPntrArrRefExp), false otherwise.
Precondition
The ref parameter must not be a null pointer.
Postcondition
If the function returns true and arrayName is not NULL, arrayName will point to the base expression of the array access.
If the function returns true and subscripts is not NULL, the vector pointed to by subscripts will contain the sequence of subscript expressions.
Note
The implementation uses a loop to traverse the chain of array references. The subscripts are inserted at the beginning of the vector to maintain the correct order of dimensions relative to the traversal.

◆ isAssignable()

bool SageInterface::isAssignable ( SgType * type)

Is a type assignable? This may not quite work properly.

Determines whether a given type can be assigned a value.

This function performs a recursive analysis of an SgType to determine its assignability. The logic evaluates the type variant and applies specific rules based on the type category:

  • For primitive types (e.g., int, float, char, etc.), pointers, and enums, it returns true.
  • For modifier types and typedefs, it recursively checks the underlying base type.
  • For class types, it checks for the presence of a public 'operator=' overload. If no such operator exists, it falls back to checking if all non-static data members of the class are themselves assignable.
  • For array types, function types, reference types, and certain other complex types, it returns false.
Parameters
typeA pointer to the SgType to be checked for assignability.
Returns
True if the type is assignable according to the defined rules; false otherwise.
Precondition
The input parameter type must not be null.
For SgClassType, the associated declaration must have a valid defining declaration.
Postcondition
The function does not modify the state of the input type.
Note
The implementation uses assertions to ensure that class declarations and definitions are valid.
The function handles C++11 specific types such as char16_t and char32_t.
If an unknown type variant is encountered, the function outputs an error to stderr and triggers an assertion failure.

◆ isAssignmentStatement()

ROSE_DLL_API bool SageInterface::isAssignmentStatement ( SgNode * _s,
SgExpression ** lhs = NULL,
SgExpression ** rhs = NULL,
bool * readlhs = NULL )

Determines if a given node represents an assignment statement and extracts its components.

Check if a SgNode _s is an assignment statement (any of =,+=,-=,&=,/=, ^=, etc)

Return the left hand, right hand expressions and if the left hand variable is also being read

This function checks whether the provided SgNode (or its underlying expression) constitutes an assignment operation (e.g., =, +=, -=, etc.). If an assignment is identified, the function extracts the left-hand side (LHS) and right-hand side (RHS) expressions. It also determines if the LHS variable is being read during the operation (which occurs in compound assignments like += but not in simple assignment =).

The implementation performs a type check on the expression variant. For compound assignment operators, it handles the extraction of the operand from assignment initializers if present.

Parameters
sThe SgNode to be inspected. Can be an SgExprStatement or an SgExpression.
lhsA pointer to an SgExpression pointer that will be populated with the left-hand side of the assignment if the node is an assignment.
rhsA pointer to an SgExpression pointer that will be populated with the right-hand side of the assignment if the node is an assignment.
readlhsA pointer to a boolean that will be set to true if the left-hand side is being read (i.e., in compound assignment operations) and false otherwise (i.e., in simple assignment).
Returns
True if the node represents an assignment statement; false otherwise.
Precondition
The pointers lhs, rhs, and readlhs must be valid (non-null) if they are to be dereferenced to store results.
Postcondition
If the function returns true, the lhs, rhs, and readlhs pointers (if provided) will point to the extracted components of the assignment.
Note
This function is adapted from the logic found in AstInterface::IsAssignment().

Check if a SgNode _s is an assignment statement (any of =,+=,-=,&=,/=, ^=, etc)

Return the left hand, right hand expressions and if the left hand variable is also being read. This code is from AstInterface::IsAssignment()

The implementation verifies that both types are class types and that the derived type is complete. It then traverses the class hierarchy of the derived class's definition to see if the base type exists within the set of ancestor classes.

ROSE_DLL_API bool SageInterface::isCanonicalDoLoop ( SgFortranDo * loop,

Check if a Fortran Do loop has a complete canonical form: Do I=1, 10, 1.

Get Fortran Do loop's key features.

Determines if a given Fortran Do loop follows a canonical structure and extracts its key features.

This function analyzes a Fortran Do loop AST node to verify if it conforms to a canonical form. A canonical loop is identified by having a valid initialization assignment (e.g., i=xx) where the loop index is of a strict integer type. The function also inspects the increment expression to determine the nature of the iteration space. If the loop is deemed canonical, the function populates the provided pointers with the loop index variable, lower bound, upper bound, step expression, and the loop body.

ubPointer to a pointer that will receive the SgExpression representing the upper bound of the loop.
stepPointer to a pointer that will receive the SgExpression representing the loop increment/step.
bodyPointer to a pointer that will receive the SgStatement representing the loop body.
hasIncrementalIterationSpacePointer to a boolean that will be set to true if the loop has an incremental iteration space, and false if the increment value is negative.
isInclusiveUpperBoundPointer to a boolean that will be set to true, as Fortran Do loops are inherently inclusive of the upper bound.
Returns
True if the loop is identified as a canonical Fortran Do loop; false otherwise.
Precondition
loop must not be NULL.
Postcondition
If the function returns true, the provided pointers (ivar, lb, ub, step, body) will point to the respective components of the canonical loop, provided they were not NULL.
Note
This function relies on the loop having a valid initialization assignment. It uses include or define logic internally via ROSE assertions.
If the increment expression is NULL, the function will trigger a ROSE_ASSERT failure.

◆ isCanonicalForLoop()

ROSE_DLL_API bool SageInterface::isCanonicalForLoop ( SgNode * loop,
SgInitializedName ** ivar = NULL,
SgExpression ** lb = NULL,
SgExpression ** ub = NULL,
SgExpression ** step = NULL,
SgStatement ** body = NULL,
bool * hasIncrementalIterationSpace = NULL,
bool * isInclusiveUpperBound = NULL )

Determines if a given loop node represents a canonical C-style for-loop.

Based on AstInterface::IsFortranLoop() and ASTtools::getLoopIndexVar().

Check if a for-loop has a canonical form, return loop index, bounds, step, and body if requested

A canonical form is defined as : one initialization statement, a test expression, and an increment expression , loop index variable should be of an integer type. IsInclusiveUpperBound is true when <= or >= is used for loop condition

This function analyzes a given SgNode to verify if it is a standard, canonical for-loop. A loop is considered canonical if it follows a predictable pattern: a single initialization statement (either a variable declaration or an assignment) involving an integer loop index, a binary comparison test against an upper or lower bound, and a standard increment/decrement expression. The function also verifies that the loop body is a structured block.

The implementation performs the following checks:

  1. Validates that the node is an instance of SgForStatement.
  2. Inspects the initialization statement to extract the loop index variable and the lower bound.
  3. Validates that the loop index variable has a strict integer type.
  4. Analyzes the loop test expression to determine the upper bound and the nature of the iteration space (inclusive vs. exclusive).
  5. Parses the increment/decrement expression to identify the step size and ensures the loop index is the operand being modified.
  6. Ensures the loop body is a structured block (single entry/single exit).
Parameters
loopA pointer to the SgNode to be inspected. Must not be NULL.
ivarPointer to a pointer that will receive the SgInitializedName of the loop index variable.
lbPointer to a pointer that will receive the SgExpression representing the lower bound.
ubPointer to a pointer that will receive the SgExpression representing the upper bound.
stepPointer to a pointer that will receive the SgExpression representing the loop step.
bodyPointer to a pointer that will receive the SgStatement representing the loop body.
hasIncrementalIterationSpacePointer to a boolean that will be set to true if the loop increments/decrements in a way that suggests a standard incremental space (e.g., <= or <).
isInclusiveUpperBoundPointer to a boolean that will be set to true if the upper bound comparison is inclusive (<= or >=) and false otherwise.
Returns
True if the loop is a canonical for-loop and meets all structural requirements; false otherwise.
Precondition
loop != NULL
Postcondition
If the function returns true, the provided pointers (ivar, lb, ub, step, body) will be populated with the corresponding loop components if they were not NULL.
Note
This function currently focuses on C-style for-loops and does not yet support Fortran-style do-loops.
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate that the loop node is not NULL.

◆ isCopyConstructible()

bool SageInterface::isCopyConstructible ( SgType * type)

Is a type copy constructible? This may not quite work properly.

Determines whether a given SgType is copy constructible.

This function performs a deep analysis of an SgType to determine if it can be copy-constructed in a C++ context. The implementation traverses the type hierarchy and examines class members, base classes, and constructor declarations.

The logic follows these rules:

  • Array types, function types, member function types, ellipsis, and decl types are not copy constructible.
  • Modifier types and typedefs are evaluated based on their underlying base types.
  • For class types, the function checks for a public copy constructor. If a user-defined constructor exists but is not a copy constructor, or if the class contains pure virtual functions, it is not copy constructible.
  • If no user-defined copy constructor is found, the function recursively verifies that all non-static data members and all base classes are themselves copy constructible.
  • Primitive types (e.g., int, char, float, etc.), pointers, and references are considered copy constructible.
Parameters
typeA pointer to the SgType to be checked for copy constructibility.
Returns
True if the type is copy constructible; false otherwise.
Precondition
The input type must not be a null pointer.
For class types, the underlying declaration must have a valid defining declaration and a valid definition.
Postcondition
The function does not modify the state of the input type.
Note
This function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate the integrity of class declarations and definitions during the traversal of class members.
The function handles C++11 specific types such as char16_t and char32_t.

Determines whether a given type or class is empty.

This function checks if a type (specifically a class or union) is "empty" based on its structural components. A class is considered empty if it contains no non-static data members with size, no virtual functions, no virtual base classes, and all its constituent members (like nested classes or unions) are also empty. The function strips typedefs and modifiers from the input type before performing the analysis.

The implementation iterates through the class members. For member functions, it ensures they are not virtual. For variable declarations, it skips static members and checks that non-static scalar members are bit fields of length 0. For non-scalar types, it recursively checks if those types are also empty. It also validates that there are no virtual base classes and that all base classes are themselves empty.

Parameters
inputTypeA pointer to the SgType to be checked for emptiness.
checkIsClassA boolean flag indicating whether the function should explicitly verify if the stripped type is a class.
Returns
True if the type is determined to be empty according to the defined criteria; false otherwise.
Precondition
inputType must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The state of the inputType and its underlying SgClassDefinition remains unchanged, though the function performs a deep inspection of the class hierarchy.
Note
This function uses recursive calls to check nested types, which may lead to deep stack usage for highly nested type definitions.
The function relies on include and define macros within the ROSE framework for type assertions and class identification.

Return true if function is overloaded.

Determines whether a given function declaration is overloaded.

This function checks if there are other function declarations with the same name within the same scope. For member functions, the search is restricted to the scope where the member function is defined (the class definition). For non-member functions, the search is restricted to the scope where the function is declared.

The implementation iterates through the members of the class definition if the input is a member function, checking for matching names in both member function declarations and template declarations.

  • For non-member functions, it does not yet implement the search logic and will trigger a ROSE_ABORT().
  • It may not catch overloads where declarations are friend functions or located in different namespace definitions (SgNamespaceDefinitionStatement).
  • If the scope is an SgDeclarationScope, the function currently returns false.
Precondition
functionDeclaration must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The function returns a boolean indicating the presence of an overload within the local scope.

Note

◆ isSameFunction()

ROSE_DLL_API bool SageInterface::isSameFunction ( SgFunctionDeclaration * func1,
SgFunctionDeclaration * func2 )

Check if two function declarations refer to the same one. Two function declarations are the same when they are a) identical, b) same name in C c) same qualified named and mangled name in C++. A nondefining (prototype) declaration and a defining declaration of a same function are treated as the same.

Determines whether two function declarations represent the same function.

There is a similar function bool compareFunctionDeclarations(SgFunctionDeclaration *f1, SgFunctionDeclaration *f2) from Classhierarchy.C

This function compares two SgFunctionDeclaration objects to check for identity or semantic equivalence based on the underlying programming language. The comparison logic varies depending on the language type:

  • For C, C99, PHP, CUDA, OpenCL, and Python, functions are considered the same if their simple names are identical.
  • For C++ and Java, functions are considered the same if the concatenation of their qualified name and their mangled name are identical, accounting for overloading and namespaces.
  • For Fortran, functions are considered the same if their simple names are identical.
Parameters
func1A pointer to the first SgFunctionDeclaration to compare.
func2A pointer to the second SgFunctionDeclaration to compare.
Returns
True if the functions are considered the same according to the language-specific logic; false otherwise.
Precondition
Both func1 and func2 must not be null. The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate this precondition.
Postcondition
The function returns a boolean value indicating the result of the comparison.
Warning
If the language of the functions is not recognized (i.e., not C, C99, PHP, CUDA, OpenCL, Python, C++, Java, or Fortran), the function prints an error to standard output and invokes ROSE_ABORT(), terminating the program.
Note
The comparison logic relies on the global language state determined by functions like is_C_language(), is_Cxx_language(), etc.

◆ IsStandardLayout()

bool SageInterface::IsStandardLayout ( const SgType *const inputType)

Determines whether a given SgType satisfies the C++ standard layout requirements.

This function performs a deep inspection of the provided type to check if it meets the criteria for a standard-layout class as defined by the C++ standard. The implementation strips modifiers, typedefs, arrays, and references from the input type to evaluate the underlying base type. It checks for several conditions including the absence of virtual functions, absence of virtual base classes, consistent access control for non-static data members, and specific rules regarding inheritance and data member distribution across the class hierarchy.

The algorithm proceeds as follows:

  1. Strips type modifiers and checks if the type is a scalar or pointer type (which are trivially standard layout).
  2. Validates that the type is a complete class type.
  3. Iterates through class members to ensure no member functions are marked as virtual.
  4. Iterates through base classes to ensure no base class is virtual.
  5. Checks that all non-static data members share the same access modifier (public, protected, or private).
  6. If the derived class has non-static data members, it ensures no ancestor classes contain non-static data members.
  7. If the derived class has no non-static data members, it ensures at most one ancestor class contains non-static data members.
  8. Recursively verifies that all base classes are also standard layout.
  9. Ensures the first non-static data member's type does not match any ancestor class type.
Parameters
inputTypeA constant pointer to the SgType to be evaluated for standard layout.
Returns
True if the type meets all standard layout criteria; false otherwise.
Precondition
The inputType must not be NULL.
The underlying class type must be a complete type (the function uses ROSE_ASSERT to verify the existence of a defining declaration and definition).
Postcondition
The function does not modify the inputType or the underlying SgType objects.
Note
This function uses ifdef DEBUG_QUADRATIC_BEHAVIOR to print debugging information regarding the size of variable collections and ancestor sets.
The function relies on the existence of a valid project context via getProject() to instantiate a ClassHierarchyWrapper.

◆ isStructurallyEquivalentAST()

bool SageInterface::isStructurallyEquivalentAST ( SgNode * tree1,
SgNode * tree2 )

Checks if two Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs) are structurally equivalent.

This function determines whether two given AST nodes, tree1 and tree2, represent structurally identical trees. The implementation utilizes RoseAst containers to provide iterators for both trees. It traverses the trees node by node, comparing the variant type of each corresponding node. If a mismatch in variant types is detected, the trees are not considered structurally equivalent.

The implementation is conditionally compiled using ifndef USE_CMAKEx. When ifndef USE_CMAKEx is active, the function performs a deep traversal using iterators to verify that every node in the first tree has a corresponding node in the second tree with the same variant type.

Parameters
tree1A pointer to the first SgNode representing the first AST to be compared.
tree2A pointer to the second SgNode representing the second AST to be compared.
Returns
True if the two ASTs are structurally equivalent (i.e., they have the same sequence of node variant types); false otherwise.
Precondition
tree1 and tree2 should be valid, non-null pointers to SgNode objects.
Postcondition
The state of the input trees remains unchanged.
Note
This function relies on the RoseAst container to facilitate iteration over the AST nodes.
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to ensure that the iterators for both trees reach the end simultaneously, implying the trees must have the same number of nodes for a successful equivalence check.

◆ isTemplateInstantiationFromTemplateDeclarationSatisfyingFilter()

template<class T>
bool SageInterface::isTemplateInstantiationFromTemplateDeclarationSatisfyingFilter ( SgFunctionDeclaration * function,
T * filter )

This function detects template instantiations that are relevant when filters are used.

Checks if a template instantiation originates from a template declaration that satisfies a given filter.

EDG normalizes some in-class template functions and member functions to be redefined outside of a class. this causes the associated template instantiations to be declared outside of the class, and to be marked as compiler generated (since the compiler generated form outside of the class declaration). ROSE captures the function definitions, but in the new location (defined outside of the class declaration). This can confuse some simple tests for template instantiations that are a part of definitions in a file, thus we have this function to detect this specific normalization.

This function is used during call graph generation to prevent the accidental filtering out of EDG-normalized function template instantiations. Because of EDG normalization, member functions may be moved outside of their class and marked as compiler-generated. This function allows the inclusion of such instantiations if their underlying template declaration passes the provided user-defined filter.

The implementation checks if the provided function is either an SgTemplateInstantiationFunctionDecl or an SgTemplateInstantiationMemberFunctionDecl. If it is, the function traverses to the first non-defining declaration to find the original template declaration and then applies the filter's operator() to that declaration.

Parameters
functionA pointer to the SgFunctionDeclaration to be inspected.
filterA pointer to a filter object (of type T) that implements operator()(SgTemplateFunctionDeclaration*) or operator()(SgTemplateMemberFunctionDeclaration*).
Returns
True if the function is a template instantiation and its underlying template declaration satisfies the provided filter; false otherwise.
Precondition
The filter parameter must be a valid pointer to an object that implements the necessary functor interface for template declarations.
Postcondition
The state of the function object remains unchanged.
Note
This function contains debug logic controlled by the define DEBUG_TEMPLATE_NORMALIZATION_DETECTION macro.

Determines whether a given type is trivial.

This function evaluates the triviality of a type by stripping modifiers, typedefs, and array dimensions to inspect the underlying base type. A type is considered trivial if it is a scalar or a pointer, or if it is a class type that meets specific criteria: it must have a trivial constructor, trivial copy constructor, trivial destructor, and trivial assignment operator. Additionally, the class must not contain virtual functions, and all non-static data members must themselves be trivial and lack in-class initializers. All base classes must also be trivial.

Parameters

Returns
True if the type is determined to be trivial; false otherwise.
Precondition
inputType must not be null.
Postcondition
The function does not modify the state of the inputType.
Note
The function uses recursive calls to check the triviality of member variables and base classes.
The function relies on the existence of a complete class definition for class types.

This function specifically checks for C++ language semantics using SageInterface::is_Cxx_language().
The implementation currently contains TODOs regarding the handling of type casting operations and typedef chains.

◆ loopCollapsing()

SgExprListExp * SageInterface::loopCollapsing ( SgForStatement * loop,
size_t collapsing_factor )

Collapses multiple nested loops into a single loop.

This function performs loop collapsing transformation on a specified nested loop structure. It takes a target loop and a collapsing factor, then replaces the nested loop hierarchy with a single loop that iterates over the combined range of the collapsed loops. The implementation normalizes the loops, calculates the total iteration space, and generates new loop index variables and interval variables to map the single collapsed index back to the original loop iterants. It also handles both incremental and decremental loop directions.

loopA pointer to the SgForStatement representing the outermost loop of the nest to be collapsed.
collapsing_factorThe number of nested loop levels to be collapsed into one.
Returns
A pointer to an SgExprListExp containing the list of all SgVarRefExp pointers to the variables that were added to the mapin clause (e.g., newly created interval and total iteration variables). Returns NULL if the collapsing factor is 1 or less, or if the target loops are not in a canonical form.
Precondition
The loops to be collapsed must be canonical for-loops.
The loops must be nested such that the target loop is the outermost loop of the sequence to be collapsed.
Postcondition
The original nested loop structure is replaced in the AST by a single for-loop.
New variable declarations for iteration counts, intervals, and the collapsed index are inserted into the scope containing the loop.
Note
The function uses global scope for generating unique variable names to prevent conflicts during potential subsequent transformations like OpenMP target data promotion.
The function relies on include and define logic via the ROSE framework for AST manipulation and relies on the ifndef USE_ROSE guard for the implementation logic.
Warning
If the target loops are not canonical, the function will print an error to stderr and return NULL.
The function performs deep copies of loop bodies and modifies the AST in place.

◆ loopUnrolling()

ROSE_DLL_API bool SageInterface::loopUnrolling ( SgForStatement * target_loop,
size_t unrolling_factor )

Unroll a target loop with a specified unrolling factor. It handles steps larger than 1 and adds a fringe loop if the iteration count is not evenly divisible by the unrolling factor.

Performs loop unrolling on a specified canonical for-loop.

This function implements a loop unrolling transformation on a given SgForStatement. The algorithm first ensures the loop is normalized and canonical. It then calculates the necessary "fringe" (the remaining iterations that do not fit into a full unrolling block) by computing the total iteration count and determining the remainder relative to the unrolling factor. The function modifies the original loop's upper bound and step size to process blocks of iterations, and replicates the loop body multiple times, adjusting the loop induction variable references within each unrolled iteration. Finally, it handles any leftover iterations using a fringe loop if the iteration count is not perfectly divisible by the unelle factor.
