unrolling_factorThe number of times the loop body is replicated in each iteration of the transformed loop.
Returns
true if the unrolling transformation was successful; false if the loop is not canonical or if an error occurs during the transformation.
Precondition
The target_loop must be a valid SgForStatement.
The loop must be in a canonical form (identifiable induction variable, lower bound, upper bound, and step).
Postcondition
If successful, the target_loop is transformed into an unrolled version with an updated step size and potentially an additional fringe loop.
The induction variable references within the unrolled bodies are automatically adjusted by the step size multiplied by the iteration offset.
Note
This function uses ifdef ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT to conditionally compile the transformation logic.
The function relies on constant folding to optimize the fringe calculation and remove unnecessary code if the fringe is not needed.
The function may introduce a new variable declaration for the fringe calculation within the scope of the target loop.

◆ mangleType()

string SageInterface::mangleType ( SgType * type)

Generate a mangled string for a given type based on Itanium C++ ABI.

Generates a unique, mangled string representation for a given SgType.

Generate a type string for a given type.

This function implements a type-mangling algorithm to create a string identifier for various SgType structures. It first attempts to retrieve a previously computed string from a global or class-level map type_string_map. If no mapping exists, the function recursively traverses the type structure to construct a mangled name based on the type's properties (e.g., scalar, modifier, pointer, reference, typedef, or array).

The implementation handles:

  • Scalar types via mangleScalarType.
  • Modifier types via mangleModifierType.
  • Pointer types by prefixing 'P' to the base type's mangled name.
  • Reference types by prefixing 'R' to the base type's mangled name.
  • Typedefs by recursively resolving the underlying base type.
  • Arrays by prefixing 'A', the element count, and an optional 'H' suffix for UPC arrays with threads, followed by the base type's mangled name.
Parameters
typeA pointer to the SgType object to be mangled.
Returns
A string containing the mangled representation of the input type. Returns "*Unhandled*" if the type category is not recognized.
Precondition
The type pointer must not be null and must point to a valid SgType object.
Postcondition
The resulting mangled string is cached in type_string_map for future lookups, and the string_type_map is updated to map the new string back to the SgType if it is a new entry.
Note
This function relies on several helper functions such as isScalarType, isSgModifierType, isSgPointerType, isSgReferenceType, isSgTypedefType, isSgArrayType, and getArrayElementCount.
Errors regarding unhandled types are printed to cerr.

Merge a variable assignment statement into a matching variable declaration statement.

Merges an assignment statement into a variable declaration as an initializer.

This function attempts to combine a separate assignment statement (e.g., x = value;) with an existing variable declaration (e.g., int x;) to create a single declaration with an initializer (e.g., int x = value;). The function performs several sanity checks to ensure the assignment targets the same variable as the declaration and that the declaration does not already possess an initializer. It also handles the migration of preprocessing information (like include or define related comments) from the assignment statement to the declaration.

Precondition

decl must not be NULL.
Postcondition
If successful, the declaration decl will contain an initializer derived from the RHS of assign_stmt.
If successful and removeAssignStmt is true, assign_stmt will be removed from its parent container.
Preprocessing information from assign_stmt is moved to decl.
Note
The function uses a fallback mechanism for variable matching: if the symbol cannot be retrieved from the symbol table, it compares the variable names instead.
The function uses SageInterface::copyExpression to ensure the RHS operand is safely duplicated for the new initializer.

e.g. int i; i=10; becomes int i=10; the original i=10 will be deleted after the merge if success, return true, otherwise return false (e.g. variable declaration does not match or already has an initializer)

◆ normalizeForLoopIncrement()

ROSE_DLL_API bool SageInterface::normalizeForLoopIncrement ( SgForStatement * loop)

Normalizes the increment expression of a for-loop to a standard addition assignment format.

This function analyzes the increment part of a given for-loop statement and attempts to transform various increment operations (such as ++, –, or -=) into a uniform addition assignment format (e.g., i += 1). The function ensures that the variable being incremented matches the variable used in the loop's test condition.

The implementation performs the following transformations:

  • V_SgPlusPlusOp (e.g., i++): Converted to i += 1.
  • V_SgMinusMinusOp (e.g., i–): Converted to i += -1.
  • V_SgMinusAssignOp (e.g., i -= s): Converted to i += (-1 * s).
  • V_SgAssignOp and V_SgPlusAssignOp: Left unchanged.

The function relies on the loop's test expression being a binary operation where the left-hand side is a variable reference, ensuring the increment target is consistent with the loop control variable.

Parameters
loopA pointer to the SgForStatement representing the for-loop to be normalized.
Returns
True if the increment expression was successfully identified and normalized; false if the loop structure is incompatible, the increment variable does not match the test expression variable, or the increment type is unsupported.
Precondition
loop must not be NULL.
Postcondition
If the function returns true, the increment expression within the loop is replaced with a normalized addition assignment expression.
Note

ROSE_DLL_API bool SageInterface::normalizeForLoopInitDeclaration ( SgForStatement * loop)

Normalize loop init stmt by promoting the single variable declaration statement outside of the for loop header's init statement, e.g. for (int i=0;) becomes int i_x; for (i_x=0;..) and rewrite the loop with the new index variable, if necessary.

Promote the single variable declaration statement outside of the for loop header's init statement, e.g. for (int i=0;) becomes int i_x; for (i_x=0;..) and rewrite the loop with the new index variable.

Promotes a single variable declaration from a for-loop init statement to the enclosing function scope.

This function transforms a for-loop with an inline variable declaration (e.g., for (int i=0; ...)) into a canonical form where the variable is declared in the function body before the loop (e.g., int i; for (i=0; ...)). The function identifies the variable declaration, creates a new declaration in the enclosing function's basic block, handles potential name collisions by appending a suffix, updates all variable references within the loop to point to the new symbol, and replaces the original declaration with an assignment statement in the loop's initialization section.

loopA pointer to the SgForStatement representing the loop to be normalized.
Returns
True if the loop was successfully normalized or was already in a state that does not require normalization (e.g., no variable declaration found). Returns false if the initialization statement is not a single variable declaration or if the initializer is too complex to be safely promoted.
Precondition

The loop must have an enclosing function definition with a valid basic block.
Postcondition
If successful, the variable declaration is moved to the start of the enclosing function's body, and the loop's init statement is updated to an assignment.
The transformation is recorded in the trans_records for potential reversal.
Note
This function handles name collisions by appending "_nom_" followed by a generated symbol counter to the variable name.
Complex initializers (e.g., SgConstructorInitializer) are skipped to maintain loop canonicality.

◆ ReductionRecognition()

ROSE_DLL_API void SageInterface::ReductionRecognition ( SgForStatement * loop,

Recognize and collect reduction variables and operations within a C/C++ loop, following OpenMP 3.0 specification for allowed reduction variable types and operation types.

Identifies OpenMP-style reduction variables within a given for loop.

This function analyzes the body of a canonical for loop to detect variables that undergo reduction operations (such as summation, finding maximum, etc.). It identifies candidate scalar variables that are live-in to the loop (not declared within the loop body) and examines their usage patterns. The algorithm checks for two primary patterns:

  1. Single appearance reduction: The variable is referenced once in a way that implies a reduction (via isSingleAppearanceReduction).
  2. Double appearance reduction: The variable is referenced exactly twice within the loop body in a pattern consistent with assignment or conditional reduction (via isAssignReduction or isIfReduction).
Parameters
loopA pointer to the SgForStatement representing the loop to be analyzed.
resultsA reference to a set of pairs, where each pair contains a pointer to the identified SgInitializedName and its corresponding OmpSupport::omp_construct_enum reduction type.
Precondition
The loop parameter must not be NULL.
The loop should be a canonical for loop for the recognition logic to proceed.
Postcondition
If reductions are found, the results set will be populated with the identified variables and their respective reduction operators.
Note
The function skips analysis if the loop is not canonical.
The function specifically filters for scalar types and excludes the loop index variable.
The function only considers variables that are live-in to the loop (i.e., their scope is not contained within the loop body).

The algorithm specifically targets SgBasicBlock nodes. Within each basic block, it iteratively scans the list of statements. If it identifies a SgGotoStatement where the target label matches the label of the very next statement in the block, the SgGotoStatement is removed from the block's statement list. ROSE_DLL_API void SageInterface::removeStatement ( SgStatement * targetStmt,

Remove a statement from its attach point of the AST. Automatically keep its associated preprocessing information at the original place after the removal. Remove a statement: TODO consider side effects for symbol tables.

Removes a statement from the AST and optionally relocates its associated preprocessing information.

This function performs the removal of a specified SgStatement from its parent statement. If the statement is deemed removable via LowLevelRewrite::isRemovableStatement, the function proceeds to detach the statement from its parent. If autoRelocatePreprocessingInfo is enabled, the function attempts to preserve the integrity of the source code representation by relocating attached comments and C/C++ preprocessor directives (such as ifdef, endif, etc.) to a surrounding statement found within the same file. This prevents the loss of preprocessing context when a statement is deleted. The function also handles the upward movement of dangling inner endif or if directives to maintain valid preprocessor nesting.

Parameters
targetStmtThe SgStatement node to be removed from the AST.
autoRelocatePreprocessingInfoA boolean flag indicating whether attached comments and preprocessor directives should be moved to a surrounding statement. Defaults to true.
Precondition
targetStmt must not be NULL (checked via ASSERT_not_null).
The function assumes a non-MSVC environment as the implementation is wrapped in ifndef _MSC_VER.
Postcondition
If the statement is removable, it is detached from its parent statement.
If autoRelocatePreprocessingInfo is true, associated preprocessing information is moved to a nearby statement in the same file or SgGlobal.
Note
This function only supports the removal of a whole statement, not an expression within a statement.
The relocation logic uses findSurroundingStatementFromSameFile() to determine the destination for relocated metadata.
Internal maps and data structures referencing the target statement are reset via resetInternalMapsForTargetStatement() to ensure consistency.

◆ replaceDefiningFunctionDeclarationWithFunctionPrototype()

ROSE_DLL_API SgFunctionDeclaration * SageInterface::replaceDefiningFunctionDeclarationWithFunctionPrototype ( SgFunctionDeclaration * functionDeclaration)

Replaces a function definition with its corresponding function prototype.

This function takes a defining function declaration and transforms it into a non-defining function prototype. It ensures that all relevant attributes such as declaration modifiers, function modifiers, special function modifiers, linkage, and extern brace status are synchronized from the original definition to the new prototype. The function also preserves the physical file ID to ensure consistent unparsing behavior.

The implementation uses buildFunctionPrototype to generate the new declaration. It handles the transfer of preprocessing information (such as include or define related metadata) and uses replaceStatement to swap the original definition with the new prototype in the AST. Special care is taken to handle template instantiations and to prevent iterator invalidation by ensuring preprocessing info is not shared between the old and new declarations.

Parameters
functionDeclarationA pointer to the SgFunctionDeclaration representing the original defining function. Must not be NULL.
Returns
A pointer to the newly created SgFunctionDeclaration representing the function prototype. Returns NULL if the input is a template instantiation or if the prototype could not be built.
Precondition
functionDeclaration != NULL.
Postcondition
If a prototype is successfully created, the original functionDeclaration is replaced in the AST by the new prototype, and the original functionDeclaration's attributes (modifiers, linkage, etc.) are replicated in the prototype.
Note
This function performs an in-place replacement in the AST.
The function ensures that if the original declaration was marked as static, the new prototype also retains the static storage modifier.
Warning
The function relies on ROSE_ASSERT to validate that the parent of the new declaration is not NULL and that preprocessing info is not duplicated between the old and new nodes.

◆ replaceExpression()

ROSE_DLL_API void SageInterface::replaceExpression ( SgExpression * oldExp,

Replace an expression with another, used for variable reference substitution and others. the old expression can be deleted (default case) or kept.

Replaces an existing expression node in the AST with a new expression node.

This function performs a structural replacement of a specific SgExpression node (oldExp) with a new SgExpression node (newExp) within the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST). It identifies the parent of the old expression and updates the appropriate child pointer in the parent node to point to the new expression. The function handles a wide variety of AST node types, including C, Matlab, Fortran, and Ada constructs, such as binary operations, unary operations, conditional expressions, for-loops, and various Ada-specific declarations and constraints.

Parameters
oldExpA pointer to the existing SgExpression node that is to be replaced.
newExpA pointer to the new SgEpxression node that will take the place of oldExp. If this is a variable reference, it will be automatically wrapped in parentheses.
keepOldExpA boolean flag indicating whether to retain the oldExp node in memory. If false, the function calls deepDelete on oldExp to prevent memory leaks. If true, the parent of oldExp is set to NULL.

newExp must not be NULL.
The parent of oldExp must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The parent of newExp is updated to be the same as the former parent of oldExp.
If keepOldExp is false, oldExp is deleted from the memory pool.
If oldExp and newExp are the same, the function returns without making changes.
Note
If newExp is an SgVarRefExp, the function calls set_need_paren(true) on it to ensure safety during code generation.

Replace a given expression with a list of statements produced by a generator.

Replaces a specific expression within the AST with a generated statement.

This function performs complex AST transformations to replace an existing expression node with a new statement structure generated by a StatementGenerator. It identifies the enclosing context of the expression (such as for-loops, while-loops, if-statements, or switch-statements) and applies specific structural rewrites to maintain the semantic integrity of the program.

For example, if the expression is part of a for-loop increment, it converts the increment into a statement added to the loop body. If the expression is a loop condition, it rewrites the loop to use a temporary boolean variable that is updated within the loop body. The function handles various control flow nodes including SgForStatement, SgWhileStmt, SgDoWhileStmt, SgIfStmt, and SgSwitchStatement.

This function relies on the existence of replaceSubexpressionWithStatement and other SageInterface utility functions.
The transformation logic is wrapped in an ifndef ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT block, meaning its behavior may differ depending on the build configuration.

◆ replaceSubexpressionWithStatement()

ROSE_DLL_API void SageInterface::replaceSubexpressionWithStatement ( SgExpression * from,

Replaces a specific subexpression within a statement with a newly generated statement.

Similar to replaceExpressionWithStatement, but with more restrictions. Assumptions: from is not within the test of a loop or ifStmt, not currently traversing from or the statement it is in

This function identifies an expression within the Sg tree and attempts to replace its occurrence with a statement produced by a StatementGenerator. The implementation checks if the expression is part of an expression statement or an assignment operator. If the expression is the root of its own statement, it replaces the statement directly. If the expression is the right-hand side of an assignment, it generates a new statement using the left-hand side as context. If the expression is nested, the function performs a transformation by splitting the expression into an initializer and converting it into an assignment, subsequently replacing the assignment statement.

This logic is wrapped in an ifndef ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT block, meaning the replacement logic is only active when not in internal frontend development mode.

Parameters
fromThe SgExpression pointer representing the subexpression to be replaced.
toThe StatementGenerator pointer used to produce the replacement statement.
Precondition
The parameter from must be a valid, non-null SgExpression.
The parameter to must be a valid, non-null StatementGenerator.
The function assumes that from is part of a valid SgStatement structure that can be retrieved via getStatementOfExpression.
Postcondition
If a direct replacement is possible (e.g., from is the root of an expression statement), the original statement in the parent node is replaced by the statement generated by to.
If the expression is part of an assignment, the assignment is transformed and replaced via replaceAssignmentStmtWithStatement.
Note
The function relies on the existence of getStatementOfExpression, getRootOfExpression, splitExpression, and convertInitializerIntoAssignment.
The function uses an assert to ensure that the transformed expression statement is not null.

Replace a given expression with a list of statements produced by a generator. The generator, when given a variable as input, must produce some code which leaves its result in the given variable. The output from the generator is then inserted into the original program in such a way that whenever the expression had previously been evaluated, the statements produced by the generator are run instead and their result is used in place of the expression. Assumptions: not currently traversing from or the statement it is in

◆ resetInternalMapsForTargetStatement()

ROSE_DLL_API void SageInterface::resetInternalMapsForTargetStatement ( SgStatement * sourceStatement)

Resets internal data structures and macro expansion states for a specific statement.

Reset internal data structures used for token-based unparsing and macro summaries based on modifications to this statement.

This function facilitates the modification of an input statement by triggering necessary updates on internal data structures that maintain references to such statements. Specifically, it handles the synchronization of macro expansion maps. If a statement associated with a macro expansion is modified or removed, this function ensures that the associated macro expansion is marked as transformed. This prevents the AST unparser from attempting to use partial or incorrect token representations of the macro, forcing instead a proper transformation output.

The implementation retrieves the enclosing source file for the provided statement. If a valid source file is found, it checks the macro expansion map. If the sourceStatement is found within the map and the macro expansion has not yet been marked as transformed, the function iterates through all statements in the macro expansion's associated statement vector. For each statement that possesses valid file information, it marks the statement as transformed and ensures it is flagged for output during code generation. Finally, the macro expansion itself is marked as transformed.

Parameters
sourceStatementA pointer to the SgStatement that is being targeted for internal map resetting.
Precondition
The sourceStatement should ideally be part of a valid AST and associated with an enclosing SgSourceFile for the macro expansion logic to execute.
Postcondition
If the sourceStatement is part of an untransformed macro expansion, all associated statements in that expansion are marked as transformed and set for code generation, and the macro expansion itself is marked as transformed.
Note
This function relies on the existence of a valid SgSourceFile. If the statement has not yet been added to the AST, the enclosing source file pointer may be NULL.
The function uses if 0 blocks for debugging purposes which are ignored during standard compilation.

Precondition
initializedNameNode must not be NULL.
The scope associated with initializedNameNode must have a valid symbol table and the symbol table must have a valid internal table.
The parent declaration of the initializedNameNode must not be NULL.
The parent declaration must be transformable (statementCanBeTransformed must return true).
Postcondition
The name of the initializedNameNode is updated to new_name.
The symbol table entry for the old name is replaced by the new_name, pointing to the same symbol.
The enclosing statement of the initializedNameNode is marked as modified and as a transformation.
All SgVarRefExp nodes in the memory pool that reference the associated symbol are marked as modified and as transformations.
Note
This function uses a RoseVisitor (RoseVisitor) to traverse the memory pool and identify all occurrences of the symbol in the AST to ensure consistency.
The function includes logic to support enum values within SgEnumDeclarations.
The return value logic (1 for success, 0 for failure) is noted as potentially reversed in the implementation comments.

Required traversal function

This function is used to initialize or reset the source position information (start of construct, end of construct, and operator position) of an IR node to a default state. This is particularly useful when nodes are built via the Build Interface and their source positions are temporarily reset before being updated with actual information from the EDG parser. The function ensures that the source position is marked as unavailable in the frontend but remains active for code generation (unparsing).

If the node is an instance of SgExpression, its operatorPosition is updated to point to a default Sg_File_Info object if it was previously NULL.
Note
This function is a performance-critical path as it is called frequently during the construction of the AST.
The function uses ROSE_ASSERT to validate the state of the node's position pointers.

◆ splitExpression() [2/2]

SgAssignInitializer * SageInterface::splitExpression ( SgExpression * from,
string newName )

Splits a complex expression into a separate variable declaration and a simpler expression.

This function performs a source-to-source transformation by extracting the logic of a given expression into a new variable declaration. It identifies the statement containing the expression and creates a new variable (either with a user-provided name or a generated unique name) to hold the result of the expression. The function also handles the recursive decomposition of complex operators such as logical AND, logical OR, and conditional expressions by breaking them down into intermediate steps.

The implementation traverses the ancestors of the expression to find operators that need to be decomposed. It uses specialized generators (e.g., AndOpGenerator, OrOpGenerator) to replace complex nodes with simpler statements. Finally, it inserts a new variable declaration into the AST and updates the original expression to reference the new variable.

Parameters
fromThe SgExpression node that is to be split and replaced by a variable reference.
newNameA string representing the name for the new variable. If an empty string is provided, a unique name is generated using a global counter.
Returns
A pointer to the SgAssignInitializer that initializes the newly created variable with the original expression's value. Returns NULL if the function is compiled under a configuration where the internal frontend development logic is disabled.
Precondition
The parameter from must not be NULL.
The expression from must be part of a valid statement structure that can be transformed (e.g., it must have a parent statement that can be identified).
Postcondition
The original expression from is replaced by a variable reference in the AST.
A new variable declaration is inserted into the AST, initialized with the original expression's value.
Note
This function uses recursion to handle cases where the expression has ancestors that also require splitting.
The function relies on ifdef ROSE_USE_INTERNAL_FRONTEND_DEVELOPMENT to determine whether the transformation logic is active.

◆ splitExpressionIntoBasicBlock()

ROSE_DLL_API void SageInterface::splitExpressionIntoBasicBlock ( SgExpression * expr)

Split long expressions into blocks of statements.

This generalizes the normal splitExpression to allow loop tests and.

Generalizes the normal splitExpression to allow loop tests by converting an expression into a basic block.

This function transforms a given SgExpression into a basic block containing an assignment statement. It utilizes an internal helper class, SplitStatementGenerator, which inherits from StatementGenerator. The implementation works by creating a new statement that assigns the value of the original expression to a target, and then wraps this assignment within a basic block structure. The function then performs an in-place replacement of the original expression with the newly generated statement using the replaceExpressionWithStatement mechanism.

Parameters
exprThe SgExpression to be split and converted into a basic block.
Precondition
expr must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgExpression object.
Postcondition
The original expression in the Sg tree is replaced by a basic block containing an assignment statement.
Note
This function is specifically designed to handle cases where expressions need to be decomposed to accommodate loop test logic.

ROSE_DLL_API SgExprStatement * SageInterface::splitVariableDeclaration ( SgVariableDeclaration * decl)

Split a variable declaration with an rhs assignment into two statements: a declaration and an assignment.

Splits a variable declaration with an initializer into a separate assignment statement.

Return the generated assignment statement, if any e.g. int i =10; becomes int i; i=10; This can be seen as a normalization of declarations

This function takes a variable declaration that contains an initializer and transforms it by removing the initializer from the declaration and creating a new expression statement that performs the assignment. This is useful for decomposing complex declarations into simpler, discrete statements. The function handles various types of initializers, including assignment initializers and aggregate initializers, by extracting the right-hand side operand.

◆ statementCanBeTransformed()

ROSE_DLL_API bool SageInterface::statementCanBeTransformed ( SgStatement * stmt)

Determines whether a given statement can undergo transformations compatible with token-based unparsing.

If header file unparsing and token-based unparsing are used, then some statements in header files used with the same name and different include syntax can't be transformed. This is currently because there is no way to generally test the resulting transformed code generated by ROSE.

This function checks if a specific SgStatement is eligible for transformation based on the unparsing capabilities of its enclosing source file. The logic primarily investigates whether the source file's unparsing configuration (specifically token-based unparsing and header file unparsing) is enabled. If the statement belongs to an included header file tracked in the EDG_ROSE_Translation::edg_include_file_map, the function verifies if that specific include file supports token-based unparsing.

Parameters
stmtA pointer to the SgStatement being evaluated for transformation eligibility.
Returns
True if the statement can be transformed (either because it is not part of a restricted header file or because its associated include file supports token-based unparsing); false otherwise.
Precondition
stmt must not be NULL, and the statement should ideally be associated with a valid SgSourceFile to ensure accurate lookup.
Postcondition
The return value indicates the transformability of the statement without modifying the state of the statement or the source file.
Note
The function relies on the EDG_ROSE_Translation::edg_include_file_mapping to resolve include files. It uses ROSE_ASSERT to ensure the retrieved source file is not NULL.
Warning
If the enclosing source file cannot be found, a warning is printed to stdout, though the function may still proceed with a default result.

If header file unparsing and token-based unparsing are used, then some statements in header files used with the same name and different include syntax can't be transformed. This is currently because there is no way to generally test the resulting transformed code generated by ROSE. NOTE: This is demonstrated by test8 in the unparse headers tests directory.

◆ suggestNextNumericLabel()

ROSE_DLL_API int SageInterface::suggestNextNumericLabel ( SgFunctionDefinition * func_def)

Suggest next usable (non-conflicting) numeric label value for a Fortran function definition scope.

Suggests the next available non-conflicting numeric label value for a Fortran function scope.

This function iterates through all symbols present in the symbol table of the provided Fortran function definition. It identifies all existing label symbols and determines the maximum current numeric label value. To avoid conflicts with existing labels, the function suggests a new value that is at least 10 units greater than the highest existing label found.

Parameters
func_defA pointer to the SgFunctionDefinition representing the scope in which the next label is to be suggested.
Returns
An integer representing the suggested next numeric label value. The default starting value is 10 if no labels are found.
Precondition
func_def must not be NULL.
The current language context must be identified as Fortran via SageInterface::is_Fortran_language().
Postcondition
The returned value will be greater than any existing numeric label value in the provided function definition's symbol table.
Warning
The returned value must not exceed 99999, as Fortran 77 labels are limited to a maximum of 5 digits.
Note
The algorithm uses a simple linear scan of the symbol table, checking each node to see if it is an instance of SgLabelSymbol.

Translates preprocessor directives within a scope to be used as C++ declarations.

This function iterates through the contents of a given scope (such as a global scope, namespace, class, or basic block) to identify and relocate C++ preprocessor directives. It distinguishes between scopes containing only declarations and scopes containing statements. For each element in the scope, it utilizes translateStatementToUseCppDeclarations to find associated directives. These directives are then inserted into the scope as individual statements. The function also manages the cleanup of the original attached preprocessing information, removing processed directives from the original statement's metadata while preserving others that should be skipped.

Precondition
scope must not be NULL.
Postcondition
The directives associated with statements within the scope are moved to the scope level as new statements, and the original attachments are updated or removed accordingly.
Note
The function uses a map to store directives temporarily to avoid iterator invalidation during the modification of the scope's contents.
The function relies on the helper function translateStatementToUseCppDeclarations to perform the underlying translation logic for individual statements.

◆ translateToUseCppDeclarations()

ROSE_DLL_API void SageInterface::translateToUseCppDeclarations ( SgNode * n)

Translates SgScopeStatement nodes to C++ declarations within a global scope.

This function performs a postorder traversal of the provided AST subtree starting at node n. It utilizes an internal class, CppTranslationTraversal, which inherits from AstSimpleProcessing. During the traversal, the function identifies nodes that are instances of SgScopeStatement. If such a node is identified as being within a global scope (SgGlobal), the function calls translateScopeToUseCppDeclarations to perform the actual translation. Currently, the implementation is designed to skip all scopes that are not global.

Parameters

n must be a valid pointer to an SgNode.

The AST subtree rooted at n is traversed in postorder, and global scopes within this subtree are processed for C++ declaration translation.
Note
The traversal is explicitly set to postorder, which may be necessary if the transformation of the AST at each scope affects the structure of the parent nodes.

Update defining and nondefining links due to a newly introduced function declaration. Should be used after inserting the function into a scope.

Updates the links between defining and non-defining function declarations within a given scope.

This function not only set the defining and nondefining links of the newly introduced function declaration inside a scope, but also update other same function declarations' links accordingly if there are any. Assumption: The function has already inserted/appended/prepended into the scope before calling this function.

This function iterates through the statements or declarations within a specified scope to identify all function declarations that refer to the same underlying function as the provided func. It establishes or updates the definingDeclaration and firstNondefiningDeclaration pointers across these related declarations. The implementation distinguishes between cases where the provided func is the defining declaration itself and cases where it is a non-defining declaration.

If func is the first non-defining declaration in the list, other identical declarations will have their firstNondefiningDeclaration updated to func if not already set.
If func is a subsequent non-defining declaration, it will attempt to inherit the firstNondefiningDeclaration from the first declaration in the identified list.
Note
This function can be computationally expensive, particularly when processing large files, as it performs identity checks (isSameFunction) across the statement list.
A warning is printed to stdout if the function symbol for the first non-defining declaration cannot be found in its associated scope.

Wraps all template instantiations within their associated namespaces.

This function traverses the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) of a given SgProject to identify all nodes that represent template instantiations. For each identified template instantiation that is a SgDeclarationStatement, the function moves the declaration into its corresponding associated namespace. The implementation uses a two-pass approach: first, it collects all relevant declaration statements into a vector to avoid iterator invalidation during AST transformation, and second, it iterates through the collected vector to perform the namespace wrapping.

Parameters

Precondition
The root pointer must be a valid, non-null pointer to an SgProject.
Postcondition
All template instantiation nodes within the provided SgProject that are SgDeclarationStatements will have been moved into their associated namespaces.
Note
This function avoids using direct iterators over the AST during the transformation phase to prevent iterator invalidation errors caused by structural changes to the AST.
